key_insight: Halide substitution strongly tunes Ca3PX3 perovskites, with iodide (Ca3PI3) emerging as the most promising solar-absorber candidate while fluoride performs poorly.
engineering_relevance: This suggests composition engineering can be used to optimize perovskite-based photovoltaic materials for higher efficiency and targeted optoelectronic performance.
method: First-principles structural analysis of Ca3PX3 (X = F, Cl, Br, I).
Electronic band-structure calculations to determine bandgap type and magnitude.
SLME-based photovoltaic screening to estimate solar cell suitability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0–3.788 eV and SLME results ranging from 0.6% for Ca3PF3 to 29.6% for Ca3PI3.
watch_item: The study is computational, so experimental stability, synthesis feasibility, and device-level performance still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
